notes: ACCESS: Tier (a) HTTP fetch succeeded fully - curl_cffi (impersonate=chrome124) + BeautifulSoup/lxml against www.seletti.it (seletti.it redirects 200 -> https://www.seletti.it/). robots.txt is a standard Shopify robots file, User-agent: * Allow: / with no Claude/Anthropic-specific disallow - tier (a)/(b) unrestricted. No Playwright or Chrome needed; site is server-rendered Shopify (Dawn-based theme) with full nav and product-count markup in the raw HTML. TREE: Built from the mega-menu drawer nav (nav.menu-drawer__navigation, Products > [Tableware, Lighting, Furniture, Objects, Textiles, Outdoor, Limited Edition, ...]). Site groups nearly everything (including Curtains, Cushions, Rugs, Cabinets, Hangers, Shelf) under one flat 'Furniture' nav bucket, and Mats/Cases under 'Objects' - website's own bucket label was not used to decide category; each node's actual product type/material was checked via its collection page and a sample product page. QTY: read from the rendered '.product-count__text' element on each collection page (e.g. '12 products'), which matched the pagination range: this is the site's own live count, not products_count API or a search-index guess. EXCLUDED and why - Textile boundary: Tablemats (55 products, material confirmed 'Cork and Polypropylene' via product characteristics block on /products/tablemat-pink-lipstick) is a rigid cork/polypropylene mat, not fabric, so excluded per textile.md material rule (the one 'Tablecloth TP Pattern Mix' item inside that collection does not change the category-level material verdict). EXCLUDED - Storage boundary: Cabinets (14) are Wardrobes/Chests-of-Drawers/Sliding-Door Cabinets, confirmed Mdf/Glass/Metal via /products/wardrobe-snakes, explicitly Furniture per site hierarchy and construction -> Furniture task, not Storage. Shelf/'Supershelf' (3) confirmed Laminate/Mdf/Wood via /products/supershelf-terrazzo, a large design shelving/bookcase furniture piece under the Furniture nav bucket -> Furniture, not Storage. Cases (61: Wash Bags, Pouches, Laptop Bags) and Travel (19: Trolleys, Travel Bags, Rucksacks, Tote Bags) and Beauty Cases (cosmetics cases inside the Beauty collection) are personal-carrying/luggage items, excluded per storage.md Storage Bags boundary (personal-carry bags are not home storage). Dustbin (7, waste bins) has no listed equivalent in storage.md's main groups and is a general household item, not a storage/organization product -> excluded. Jewels and Memorabilia collections were checked and contain jewelry/decor objects only, no jewelry organizers or storage items found. INCLUDED - Textile: Curtains, Cushions, Rugs, Mats all verified as genuine fabric/textile products via sample product 'characteristics' blocks (e.g. Mat Shit = Polyester; Cushion Bowling = Plume/Polyester padding) despite Seletti's internal Shopify product-type tag sometimes reading 'Furniture' or 'Objects' - per textile.md's explicit Cushion/Curtain/Rug examples, PRIMARY PRODUCT TYPE overrides the site's internal type tag. 'Textiles' (39 products, the Dondi x Seletti collab, also linked as 'Seletti x Dondi' under Limited Edition) is a genuine home-textile collection (cotton aprons, oven mitts/pot holders, cotton tablecloths, table runners, tea towels, a cotton pareo) reached from a standalone top-level 'Textiles' nav link with no further sub-navigation, so its own collection URL was recorded per the parent-URL exception for categories with no subcategories. INCLUDED - Storage: Hangers (19: whimsical resin wall-hooks shaped like a cactus/mushroom/snail/sprout, material confirmed Resin via /products/cactus) - genuine hanging/organization function (coat/item hooks) matching storage.md's Closet & Wardrobe Storage 'Hanging Storage'/'Hanging Organizers', but flagged LOW confidence because Shopify's own internal product-type tag for these items reads 'Objects' (decorative) rather than storage/furniture, so this sits on the Storage vs Decorative-Home-Accessories boundary - recommend manual review. No duplicate research was done between the Textile and Storage passes; every collection/product page was loaded once and classified for both arrays from the same HTML.
